name: poteto-mode
purpose: Apply poteto's deliberate worker routing, principle-grounded decisions, concise detailed prose, simple code and verified playbooks.
triggers: Requests to work in this style
Matched playbook or rigor needed on a new task; exclude casual turns and opt-out
inputs: Authorized task and active workflow owner
Full mode, chosen playbook and applied principle leaves
Observed tools, permissions, role configuration and exact assignment revision
Actual selected-playbook helper contracts, owned log or store paths, exact heads and remaining watch budget
outputs: Selected playbook todos with explicit skipped steps
Four-item throughput checkpoint, reviewed artifacts and evidence
Decision explanation naming only principles read in this session
Explicit reduced or blocked capabilities and open decisions
Inspected helper receipts and explicit setup, delivery and independent-review gates
ordinaryExample: For a scoped feature, read the full mode and Feature playbook, name its data shape, write the checkpoint, assign an authorized fresh worker and inspect its resulting diff before reporting evidence.
capabilityLimits: Companion deslop, no-comments, create-skill and control tools require discovered support; missing gates remain visible.
Fresh workers and model diversity require observed capabilities; sequential fallback is reduced capability.
Metadata does not register host modes or agents.
All 23 bundled routes and original 26 local references are present. Reading and structural checks do not establish execution or host behavior.
No autonomy grant overrides authorization or permissions.
Bootstrap never installs. Missing pinned dependencies block CLI execution; isolated snapshot tests support only that snapshot.
Watcher events require kind, terminal and reason inspection at pinned heads. Helper deadlines are not hard wall-clock guarantees.
Orch bookkeeping does not enforce assignment identity, full SHA syntax, evidence existence, worker completion, verifier precedence or permissions. Callers own those gates.
A no-spawn worker returns its own scoped diff to the lead; it does not satisfy the lead independent-review gate.
Helper setup guide contains historical setup statements. Future setup needs separate exact-copy authorization.
